text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn confirmed reports that Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo has submitted his resignation, however, he wants to hold consultations for one or two weeks before accepting the resignation. @

- The Parliament opened a debate on amending the National Bank act, under which the central budget would in January acknowledge a sizeable part of the National Bank's external debts in the form of foreign currency debt owed by the budget to the Bank.
- Parliament's defence committee on Wednesday heard a report on the transformation of the armed forces, ahead of today's cabinet discussion of the matter. @
- Marta Tocsik, saying that criminal proceedings are underway against her, yesterday refused for the fifth time to appear before the parliamentary commission investigating her 804 million forint fee.
- Human Rt., one of the largest suppliers of hospitals, has suspended its moratorium on shipping medicine to hospitals until November 22, the date when hospitals must repay their debts.
- Hungary has been admitted to the export credit and export credit guarantee group of the commercial committee of OECD, said Industry Minister Szabolcs Fazekas. @

- A total of 1.6 billion forints, five times the 1996 sum, will be available for scientific research and technical developments and operation of university laboratories next year, Culture and Education Minister Balint Magyar announced.
- A few hours after the new bill on the mortgage fund was passed Tuesday, Austria's Generali group announced its intention to found a bank in Hungary to finance home purchases. @
NEPSZAVA
- A German government state secretary made a telephone pledge to the effect that two-thirds of the hazardous waste stranded at Letenye since late September will shortly be reshipped to Germany.

- A total of 2,818 new foreign interest businesses were registered in the first nine months of the year, with combined registered capital of 34.8 billion forints, the Central Statistics Office reports. @
- K&H bank has issued an international co-branded card under the name Fotex Visa Card, probably the first such instrument in Eastern Europe.
- The Hungarian employees of IAP Hungary Kft, a US company catering to IFOR forces at the Taszar air base, have won a lawsuit filed against the company at the Kaposvar Labour Court.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Yesterday's meeting of the Joint Venture Association criticised a government plan to eliminate the 25 percent personal income tax preference currently available for foreign employees, as part of the 1997 personal income tax bill. @
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The State Securities and Stock Exchange Supervision has prolonged the moratorium on trading Magyar Hitel Bank shares for a further two days pending an announcement on which of ABN Amro and Creditanstalt have won the bank's privatisation tender.
- The first units of Hungary's second largest underground gas storage facility will be inaugurated by MOL on Friday in Zsana, south central Hungary. @
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. could invite tenders for the Eger-based electronic equipment manufacturer Vilati this year.
